lede: Gladewater is a straight shot west on US 80 from our Longview base. We mow, trim, plant, build and fix drainage here with the same crew every time.
intro: Yard Dog Landscapes provides landscaping and lawn care in Gladewater, TX, out of our home base in Longview. We're a family-owned company started in 2017 by Miller Maines, and Miller and the same crew of four do every job themselves, with no subcontractors. We carry full insurance and a 5.0 Google rating across {{REVIEWS}} reviews. A free walkthrough and a written, itemized estimate usually come within a day. Request a free quote anytime.

Gladewater sits where US 80 crosses US 271, mostly in Gregg County with part of town in Upshur County. The older homes around downtown sit under mature pines and hardwoods, with shaded lawns and leaf-filled beds every fall. Outside town the lots open up into acreage with woods, fence lines and long drives, and some properties sit out toward Lake Gladewater. The ground is the same sandy loam over clay found across this part of East Texas.

That mix shapes the work. In town that usually means mowing, hedges, leaf cleanup and bed refreshes under big trees. On the larger properties it's more about keeping a big lawn cut on a steady schedule, trimming along fences and ditches and solving drainage across a whole lot instead of one corner. Gladewater is a little farther out than White Oak, so we'll be straight with you about how often we can be there before you sign up.

yard_notes.title: Big trees in town
yard_notes.text: Older Gladewater streets have tall pines and hardwoods over the yards. Expect a heavy leaf drop, shaded St. Augustine and beds that need shade plants and mulch more than sun lovers.

yard_notes.title: Acreage outside town
yard_notes.text: Larger lots past the edge of town mean longer mowing days, more fence line to trim and drainage that has to be solved across a whole property.

yard_notes.title: Sand over clay
yard_notes.text: Like most of Gregg County, Gladewater ground is sandy on top with clay below. It drains well until the top saturates, and then low spots stay wet after a long rain.

faq.q: Do you serve the Upshur County side of Gladewater?
faq.a: Yes. We cover all of Gladewater, on both the Gregg and Upshur County sides, plus the rural properties around town. Upshur County is part of our regular service area.

faq.q: Is Gladewater too far out for weekly mowing?
faq.a: No. It's an easy drive west on US 80 from Longview. Weekly mowing starts at $65 per visit for a typical yard, and larger acreage is priced on its own after we walk it.

faq.q: How much does landscaping cost in Gladewater?
faq.a: Bed refreshes start at a few hundred dollars, and most landscaping and planting projects run $900 to $3,600. Mulch refreshes run $600 to $2,400, hedge trimming $150 to $800 and drainage projects $2,000 to $3,750. Your exact price comes in writing after a free walkthrough.

faq.q: Do you work on properties near Lake Gladewater?
faq.a: Yes, on the land side: lawns, beds, retaining walls, drainage and cleanups. Docks, boathouses and seawalls are not our work.

service_angles.lawn-maintenance: Gladewater lawns run from small in-town yards to acreage outside town, and we price and schedule each one on its own. In town we mow, edge and blow clean around beds and walks, and on bigger properties we add string trimming along fence lines, ditches and outbuildings. Typical residential yards start at $65 per visit.
service_angles.leaf-removal: Gladewater's older streets and wooded lots get buried in oak leaves and pine straw every fall, and leaves settle in ditches and along fence lines where they block water. We clear lawns, beds, drives and those edges, then haul it away, and big wooded properties may need more than one pass. Leaf removal is priced after a walkthrough.
service_angles.fertilization: Gladewater's sandy topsoil lets nutrients wash through quickly, especially after a long rain. We test the soil, correct pH with lime when it's needed and spread feedings through the season instead of one heavy shot, finishing with a fall winterizer. Visits start from about $190, and bigger lawns are priced by size.
service_angles.hedge-trimming: Older Gladewater homes often have long-established hedges along property lines, foundations and front walks. We shape them on a steady schedule, take overgrown ones back in stages when they need it and haul off every clipping. Most hedge trimming jobs in town land between $150 and $800.
service_angles.tree-shrub-care: Plenty of established Gladewater yards have shrubs and ornamental trees that outgrew their space: crepe myrtles crowding a roofline, hollies swallowing a walk, small trees leaning into a fence. We prune by species and season, remove small trees and shrubs that are past saving and pick up storm limbs. It's all quoted after we walk the property.
service_angles.tree-planting: On open acreage around Gladewater, new trees go into full sun with no shade nearby, so the first two summers decide everything. We pick trees suited to East Texas, plant in the fall window, build a watering basin and mulch ring and leave you an aftercare plan. Planting is quoted after a walkthrough.
service_angles.sod-installation: Gladewater sod jobs range from patching a shaded in-town yard to covering a big open lawn after construction or a drainage fix. We prep, level and amend the sandy topsoil first, lay tight seams and match St. Augustine or Bermuda to the sun. Sod is sold by the pallet, and most projects come in between $1,500 and $4,700.
service_angles.landscaping: In Gladewater, landscaping often means bringing an older yard back: foundation beds reset, overgrown shrubs replaced, a clean edge cut where grass has crept in. On bigger properties it might mean planting along a long drive or around the house to frame it. Small refreshes start at a few hundred, and most projects run $900 to $3,600.
service_angles.flower-bed-installation: Gladewater beds under mature trees deal with shade and root competition, while beds on open acreage bake in full sun. We amend the sandy soil, set the grade away from the house and choose plants for the exact light each bed gets, then finish with mulch to hold the moisture. Fall and early spring are the best planting windows.
service_angles.mulch-installation: With heavy tree cover over many Gladewater yards, mulch breaks down and gets buried under leaves faster than people expect. We clear the old layer, re-cut the edges and spread 1 to 1.5 inches evenly, kept off trunks and siding. A typical bed refresh here runs $600 to $2,400.
service_angles.hardscaping: Gladewater patios and walkways get the same build we use everywhere: dig out, compact a crushed stone base, set the stone or pavers level and pitch them away from the house. On larger lots that might be a path from the drive to the back door or a patio with a fire pit. Hardscape projects mostly run $3,100 to $9,100.
service_angles.retaining-walls: Where a Gladewater yard slopes toward the house or a drive cuts into a bank, a wall holds the soil and creates level ground. We build segmental block and natural stone walls on a compacted base below grade, with gravel backfill and a drain behind them. Short garden walls start at a few thousand dollars, and most walls run $3,000 to $19,000.
service_angles.drainage: On bigger Gladewater properties, water problems often start upslope: a neighboring field, a road ditch or a long drive sending runoff toward the house. We find where it starts, then cut swales, regrade or run French drains to carry it past the house to a real outlet. Most drainage projects here run $2,000 to $3,750, with small fixes from about $450.
service_angles.christmas-lights: Gladewater sits well within our install range from Longview. We supply warm white or color C9 lines custom-cut to the roofline, install them, take them down after the season and store them, for homes and storefronts. Quotes come from a photo mock-up of the building, and most homes start at $900.
service_angles.irrigation: Gladewater properties often have more ground than anyone wants to water, so we focus the system where it counts: the lawn and beds around the house, zoned by sun and shade, with drip in the beds. The open acreage stays on rain.

lawn-maintenance.q: Do you mow larger acreage around Gladewater?
lawn-maintenance.a: Yes. Larger lots get priced after a walkthrough, since the $65-per-visit starting price is for a typical residential yard. We'll look at how much is lawn, how much is trim work along fences and ditches, and how often it needs cutting.

leaf-removal.q: Will you clear leaves out of my ditch in Gladewater?
leaf-removal.a: Yes. Leaves and limbs that collect in a front ditch or around a culvert block water and can back it up into the yard. We clear them out as part of a cleanup and haul everything off.

fertilization.q: When should I start fertilizing my Gladewater lawn?
fertilization.a: Not too early. Wait until nighttime lows hold above 60 degrees, usually late April. Feeding before the grass is actively growing mostly wastes product. From there we follow up in early July, early September and with an October winterizer.

hedge-trimming.q: Can you cut back a hedge that's taken over my Gladewater walkway?
hedge-trimming.a: Yes. If it's badly overgrown we'll take it back in stages so it fills in instead of going bare. Some older shrubs handle a hard cut in late winter, and a few are better replaced. We'll tell you which.

tree-shrub-care.q: Do you clean up storm limbs in Gladewater?
tree-shrub-care.a: Yes. After a storm we pick up downed limbs and branches, trim broken ends back to clean cuts and haul it off. A large tree down on a house or a power line is a job for a tree service or the utility.

tree-planting.q: What shade trees grow well around Gladewater?
tree-planting.a: Native oaks like Shumard and willow oak do well in this part of East Texas, and bald cypress handles wetter ground. Pecans need plenty of room. We'll match the tree to the spot, the soil and how big it will get.

sod-installation.q: Can you sod over a spot you just drained in Gladewater?
sod-installation.a: Yes. After a French drain or regrade, we put sod back over the trench and any reshaped ground so it doesn't wash before it roots. Matching the existing grass keeps the repair from standing out.

landscaping.q: Can you redo old foundation beds in Gladewater?
landscaping.a: Yes. We pull out what's overgrown or dying, fix the grade so water runs away from the house, amend the soil and replant with shrubs sized for the space. Refreshes start at a few hundred dollars, and bigger redesigns usually run $900 to $3,600.

flower-bed-installation.q: What plants hold up in full sun on open Gladewater lots?
flower-bed-installation.a: Lantana, salvia, Knock Out roses, daylilies and esperanza all take East Texas sun and heat. We plant them in amended soil, mulch them and set the bed so it drains.

mulch-installation.q: Should mulch go up against my house in Gladewater?
mulch-installation.a: No. Keep it pulled back a few inches from the siding or brick and from tree trunks. Mulch piled against a wall holds moisture where you don't want it and gives insects a path to the house. We spread it even and leave that gap.

hardscaping.q: Do you build walkways in Gladewater?
hardscaping.a: Yes. Flagstone, pavers or stepping stones set in gravel or sod, from the drive to the front door or across the backyard. Every one sits on a compacted base so it stays level.

retaining-walls.q: What's the difference between a garden wall and a structural wall?
retaining-walls.a: A garden wall is short and mostly shapes beds or levels a small area. A structural wall holds back a real load of soil, so it needs a deeper base, geogrid on taller builds and drainage behind it. Short garden walls start at a few thousand dollars, and tall structural walls can run $20,000 or more.

drainage.q: Can you handle drainage across a whole Gladewater property?
drainage.a: Yes. On larger lots we look at the whole slope instead of only the wet corner, and may combine swales, regrading and French drains. Full systems usually run $3,000 to $4,500, and large properties can go higher.

christmas-lights.q: Is Gladewater close enough for standard Christmas light pricing?
christmas-lights.a: Yes. Gladewater falls inside our standard install range, so most homes start at $900. The higher $1,800 starting price only applies to installs more than an hour from Longview.

irrigation.q: Do you install sprinkler systems in Gladewater?
irrigation.a: Yes. We install and repair sprinkler systems in Gladewater and out toward the lake, under Texas Licensed Irrigator Matthew Maines, LI0006657, and we pull the permit the job requires. Pricing comes after a free walkthrough.
